title: 4-Dimensional Reflection High Energy Electron Diffraction on 2-Dimensional Materials in a Scanning Electron Microscope
content: Mono- and multi-layer 2-dimensional (2D) materials are commonly grown directly on substrates using chemical vapor deposition techniques or stamped from a larger bulk crystal to a desired substrate for various applications. In some cases, 2D material properties of interest can be gleaned without removing the sample from the substrate. For example, Raman spectroscopy is used for defect characterization, layer number measurements, and so on [1]. However, some parameters of interest such as grain size and orientation distributions are difficult, if not impossible, to measure without removing the sample from the substrate, transferring the film to an electron transparent substrate, and using techniques such as 4-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM), to map and quantify grain size and orientation, for example [2,3]. Removing 2D films from the substrate for characterization is not ideal for some applications since it is not feasible to reuse the film. Therefore, information like grain orientation becomes impractical to incorporate into device optimization and manufacturing processes. To that end, we demonstrate how a conventional scanning electron microscope (SEM) and reflection high energy electron diffraction (RHEED) can be used together (i.e., RHEED-in-SEM) to characterize various 2D materials without removing the 2D films from substrates. Although RHEED has been implemented in an SEM with notable success [4], we take the combined techniques further and demonstrate how to implement 4D RHEED in an SEM which conceivably enables imaging, diffraction, grain size and orientation distribution measurements. The primary intent of this contribution is to provide proof-of-concept for the technique with suggestions for further refinement and future implementation.
